I have been farming this land for 45 years. My father farmed it before me. I know every corner of my 16.1 mu — which stretches drain a bit fast, where the soil is heavier. Two of us in the house now, so I need to be realistic about labor. I cannot do everything I could do at 40.

My main system is wheat-maize on about 10 mu. That rotation is reliable. Wheat goes in October, maize takes over after the June harvest. Same fields. I have been doing this my whole life. The wheat and maize bring in the most money and feed the family.

I keep about 3 mu of cotton. The price has been up and down, but I know cotton. I grew up with it. The pesticide work is heavy — I spray many times for bollworm and aphids — but I know when to look and what to do. I will not give it up yet.

The remaining 3 mu I split between millet, mung bean, and peanut. Millet and mung bean we mostly eat ourselves and give to family. Peanut I can sell locally. These crops need less water and less work than cotton, which matters at my age.

For fertilizer, I use compound fertilizer at planting and urea as topdressing. I probably put on a bit more nitrogen than some people say I should — I have always done it this way and my yields are decent. My well gives me good irrigation access. Wheat I water at least 3-4 times: before winter, at jointing, at heading, and sometimes at grain filling if it is dry. Maize maybe 2-3 times depending on rain.

For seed, I use improved wheat varieties — the county station has been promoting them and I switched maybe 15 years ago, yields went up. Maize I always buy hybrid. For the small crops like millet and mung bean, I still use my own saved seed or local traditional varieties. Peanut I buy improved.

Tillage is rotary for most crops. For maize after wheat I sometimes go straight in without deep ploughing — saves time and my back.
